Embedded fonts are smaller, and every one is now embedded in the form ISO 32000-1 allows. Each TrueType subset
carries only the glyphs a document drew, renumbered. A new option leaves out the hinting inside each glyph for a
smaller file still. A face with PostScript outlines (a CFF `.otf`) now goes in as OpenType, which it never did.

**Upgrade if your documents use a large system face such as Arial, or a face with PostScript outlines.** Pages look
exactly as before: an invoice set in Arial was compared at 100% in Edge and in Firefox, and no pixel changed. The
bytes of every PDF change, because every subset is renumbered. Nothing was removed or renamed. One thing is now
refused that was written before: a face with PostScript outlines keyed by CID (see below).

## Smaller fonts, the same pages

A subset used to keep the numbering of the whole face, so a face of thousands of glyphs paid for all of them in
every document. The glyphs a document draws are now renumbered, and a small map in the PDF takes the codes on the
page to them. Text still copies, searches and reads aloud as before.

| Document | 0.7.0 | 0.8.0 |
|---|---|---|
| An invoice in Arial, regular and bold | 66.2 KB | 50.9 KB |
| The same, hinting left out (below) | | 29.5 KB |
| Every sample the test suite writes, together | 2.02 MB | 1.87 MB |

The more glyphs a face has, the more it saves: for a regular and a bold drawing about seventy characters, the bundled
faces save from 2.6 KB (Mulish) to 13 KB (Noto Sans Display), and Arial 15 KB.

## Leaving out the hinting

A hinted face carries a small program in each glyph that fits its outline to the pixel grid at small sizes on
screen. Leaving it out roughly halves what Arial costs again:

| Where | How |
|---|---|
| C# | `new PdfBackend(fonts) { Hinting = false }` |
| CLI | `frisket render ... --no-hinting` |
| Native library | `"hinting": false` in the options, `font_hinting` in the C++ wrapper, `FontHinting` in the Pascal one |

It stays **on by default**, because what it costs depends on the reader. Edge, whose viewer is Acrobat's engine,
drew the invoice identically without it. Firefox did not: at 8 pt, "Montant dû" read "Montant d0", the accent run
into the letter. Turn it off when your documents are read in Acrobat or Edge, or printed.

The face's own hinting tables (`cvt`, `fpgm`, `prep`) always stay. ISO 32000-1 9.9 requires them in the embedded font
whenever the face has them, and PDF/A-3 and PDF/UA-1 both embed fonts by that clause. veraPDF does not check it, so a
tool that drops them produces files that validate and do not conform.

None of the faces bundled with Frisket is hinted, so the option changes nothing for them.

## Fixed: faces with PostScript outlines

A face with PostScript outlines was embedded under `/FontFile2` and read by a `CIDFontType2`, which ISO 32000-1 keeps
for TrueType outlines. veraPDF passed it, and readers built on FreeType drew it anyway, which is why nobody saw it. It
now goes in as OpenType under `/FontFile3`, read by a `CIDFontType0`. Every glyph is kept, and the tables a PDF never
reads (kerning, ligatures, glyph positioning) are left out: the bundled Glametrix goes from 188 to 73 KB before
compression.

A face with PostScript outlines **keyed by CID** - most Chinese, Japanese and Korean `.otf` faces - is now refused
when a PDF is written, with a message naming the face. A PDF chooses such a face's glyphs through its charset, which
this writer does not read, so the text could come out as other characters. Use the TrueType build of the face. The
HTML proof and SVG output still draw it.

## Fixed: `--no-subset` / `Subset = false`

A face embedded whole no longer carries its `cmap` table, which ISO 32000-1 forbids in a TrueType font used as a
CIDFont, nor a digital signature that no longer matched its bytes. A font collection (`.ttc`) now embeds the face it
was read for, not the whole collection.

## Worth checking

- **Every PDF changes bytes, and no page changes.** If you compare produced PDFs to stored ones byte for byte, store
  them again.
- **A CID-keyed `.otf` face now stops a PDF from being written.** The message names it.
- **If a reader ever refuses a font**, `Subset = false` (`--no-subset`, `"subset": false`) still embeds each face whole.

veraPDF passes PDF/A-3B and PDF/UA-1 on a document holding a renumbered subset, a subset without its hinting and a
face with PostScript outlines, and on the Arial invoice with the hinting kept and left out. Each glyph of an embedded
subset is checked against the face it came from, accented letters through the glyphs they are built from.
